in_arabic.name: كوتيبة
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مذكر يعني المُكَمِّل أو المُتمم للشيء
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم كوتيبة هو اسم مذكر عربي الأصل، ويعني المُكَمِّل أو المُتمم للشيء، وقد ورد في بعض الأحاديث النبوية، ويحمل دلالة على الإكمال والتمام في مختلف المجالات، خاصة في الإيمان والعمل الصالح.

in_urdu.name: کوتیبہ
in_urdu.meaning: کوتیبہ کا مطلب ہے مکمل کرنے والا یا کسی چیز کو مکمل کرنے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: کوتیبہ ایک عربی ಮೂಲ کا مذکر نام ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے مکمل کرنے والا یا کسی چیز کو مکمل کرنے والا۔ یہ نام بعض النبوی احادیث میں ذکر ہوا ہے، اور یہ ایمان اور عمل صالح میں تکمیل اور تمام ہونے کی دلالت کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: कुतीबा
in_hindi.meaning: कुतीबा का अर्थ है किसी चीज़ को पूरा करने वाला या संपূর্ণ करने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: कुतीबा एक अरबी मूल का पुल्लिंग नाम है, जिसका अर्थ है किसी चीज़ को पूरा करने वाला या संपूर्ण करने वाला। यह नाम कुछ नबवी हदीसों में उल्लेखित है, और यह विश्वास और अच्छे कार्यों में पूर्ति और पूर्णता की प्रतीक है।

in_pashto.name: کوټیبه
in_pashto.meaning: کوټیبه د مکملونکي یا بشپړونکي شی معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: کوټیبه د عربي اصل مذکر نوم دی، چې معنی يې د مکملونکي یا بشپړونکي شی دی. دا نوم په ځینو نبوي احادیثو کې راغلی دی، او دا په ایمان او نیکو کارونو کې د تکمیل او تمامتیا دلالت کوي.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kutaiba holds a significant impact on Islamic history as it is the name of several prominent figures in the Islamic world. Kutaiba ibn Khalid was an early Muslim general and a commander under the caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab during the Islamic expansion in the 7th century. He led numerous military campaigns against Christian and Byzantine forces, contributing to the early Islamic conquests. Kuteibah Al-Hilali Al-Khuzai is another famous figure with the name, who was a major figure during the Umayyad period and is most known for his role in the Second Fitna. His military prowess and loyalty to the Islamic state played a crucial role in ensuring the stability and preservation of the Muslim community during a time of political turmoil.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Kutaiba holds significance in the golden age of Islamic history when courage, strength, and loyalty were essential qualities for maintaining the unity of the Islamic community. The name serves as a reminder of the spirits of mutual support, valor, and determination, which were exhibited by the early Muslims during their battles against seemingly invincible enemies. By invoking the spirit of Kutaiba, we are inspired to embody the qualities of resilience and bravery in our daily lives, striving for success in the face of adversity. Ultimately, the name turns the past into a source of inspiration for the future, guiding us towards a path of victory and honor.

historical_references.reference: Kutaiba ibn Abi Rabah al-Thaqafi was a prominent Arab general in the early Islamic army under the Rashidun Caliphs, serving under Caliphs Abu Bakr and Umar. He rose to prominence through his military campaigns against the Byzantines and the Persians, most notably during the Battle of Ajnadayn in 634 AD, where he led the right wing of the Muslim army and was instrumental in defeating the Byzantine forces led by the Emperor Heraclius.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic military campaigns against the Byzantines and Persians

historical_references.reference: Kutaiba ibn Abi Rabah is also known for his conquest of Khuzestan (in modern-day Iran) in 632 AD, which marked the beginning of Muslim rule in the region. He was appointed as the first Arab governor of the area and established a military base at Al-Ahwaz (Ahvaz). His governance was marked by his fair treatment of the local population and his efforts to integrate them into the Islamic state, which contributed to the stability and success of the early Islamic expansion into the region.
historical_references.context: Muslim conquest of Khuzestan and establishment of early Islamic rule

modern_usage.modern_context: Kutaiba ibn Abi Dhiyyab al-Ka'bi (642-712 AD) is a significant figure in Islamic history, prominently remembered for his military tactics and leadership skills. Known for his bravery and strategic prowess, Kutaiba led several successful campaigns against the Byzantine and Persian Empires, expanding the Islamic State's territories during the Umayyad Caliphate's rule. His military tactics, including the famous 'flying squadrons' and 'feigned retreats,' influenced later Islamic military strategies. Kutaiba's legacy continues to inspire modern discussions on Islamic history, military tactics, and leadership. Platforms like Wikipedia provide extensive information on Kutaiba's life and achievements, while Twitter and Reddit host lively debates among scholars and enthusiasts about his tactics and leadership style.
